family: Stochastic portfolio theory / rebalancing (volatility) premium: Fernholz excess growth rate, Shannon's demon (constant-mix vs buy-and-hold), functionally generated portfolios (diversity-weighted p in (0,1), entropy-weighted, equal-weight as p->0), relative arbitrage vs the cap-weighted market, and the dollar-neutral long-FGP / short-market book.
thesis: The tactic is to hold a fixed (or generating-function-determined) weight vector and mechanically sell relative winners / buy relative losers at each rebalance, so that the portfolio's log-growth exceeds the weighted average log-growth of its constituents by the excess growth rate gamma* = 1/2 (sum_i w_i sigma_i^2 - sigma_p^2) — a pure second-moment quantity that needs no forecast. With crypto inputs (sigma 60-100%/yr, rho 0.5-0.8, N 20-60) gamma* is 3-25%/yr (central ~11%/yr) and the constant-mix turnover is only ~7x/yr daily (0.6-1.5%/yr at 21 bp), so cost is NOT what kills it. What kills it for these goalposts is what gamma* is: (a) it is a growth-rate (variance-drag) term, not an arithmetic expected return — the per-decision Sharpe the repo grades on sees it only as lower variance; (b) versus buy-and-hold of the same initial weights it is zero to first order under iid returns (B&H captures the same Jensen convexity by drifting), positive only with cross-sectional mean reversion at the rebalance horizon (a forecast) and negative under momentum; (c) the absolute return of every long-only version is market beta + gamma*, and the record already holds the daily-rebalanced 1/N PIT book at gross Sharpe -0.40 FULL / -2.54 BEAR22; (d) the long-diversity/short-market 'relative arbitrage' reduces to a bet that market concentration will not rise — in 2022 ex-stablecoin BTC dominance rose ~41%->46.5% and small alts fell ~80% vs BTC -64%, so the relative book lost ~30% of the long leg (about -15% dollar-neutral) before costs; 2018 had the same sign. Under the no-free-lunch taxonomy the family draws on source (3) the rebalancing premium in log-growth terms, but everything it can put on the goalposts' scoreboard is source (2) beta / small-coin tilt plus an implicit source (1) anti-concentration or mean-reversion forecast. Its legitimate residual is source (4): a bounded-turnover, auditable execution layer for a book whose edge comes from elsewhere.
math:
EXCESS GROWTH. gamma* = 1/2 (sum_i w_i sigma_i^2 - sigma_p^2). Equal weights, homogeneous sigma, common rho: sigma_p^2 = sigma^2 [1/N + (1-1/N) rho] => gamma* = 1/2 sigma^2 (1-rho)(1-1/N). Inputs -> result: (sigma,rho,N)=(0.60,0.80,20): 0.5*0.36*0.20*0.95 = 3.4%/yr; (0.80,0.65,40): 0.5*0.64*0.35*0.975 = 10.9%/yr; (1.00,0.50,60): 0.5*1.0*0.5*0.983 = 24.6%/yr; 2022 crash regime (0.85,0.80,40): 7.0%/yr. Vol heterogeneity (half at 60%, half at 120%): sum w sigma^2 = 0.90 vs mean-sigma^2 0.81, adds ~1-2 pp. Shannon 50/50 risky/cash: gamma* = 1/2 w(1-w) sigma^2 = 0.125*0.64 = 8%/yr at sigma=0.8.
TURNOVER (repo convention sum|delta pos| per unit capital, trader/backtest.py:224). Constant mix at interval dt trades sum_i w_i |r_i - r_p| ~= 0.8 * sigma_idio * sqrt(dt), sigma_idio = sigma sqrt(1-rho). (0.80,0.65): sigma_idio = 0.473/yr = 2.48%/day -> daily 1.98%/day = 7.2x/yr -> 21 bp costs 1.5%/yr; weekly 5.25%/rebalance = 2.7x/yr -> 0.57%/yr; +-20% relative no-trade bands: trade rate ~ sigma_idio^2/(2 delta) = 0.224/0.4 = 0.56x/yr -> 0.12%/yr. Trend book for comparison: 56.6x/yr -> 11.9%/yr (PORTFOLIO_RESULT.md). Net of 21 bp roughly 85% (daily) / 94% (weekly) / 97% (bands) of gamma* survives. Sharpe-equivalent of a 10%/yr gamma* on a book with sigma_p = 0.8*sqrt(0.025+0.634) = 65%/yr: (0.10/365)/(0.65/19.1)*19.1 = 0.15 — and it does not even enter the arithmetic mean.
WHY IT IS NOT A PREMIUM OVER B&H. CM log growth = sum w_i g_i + gamma*. B&H log growth = log sum_i w_i e^{g_i T} >= sum w_i g_i T. With idiosyncratic log-variance s^2 = sigma^2 (1-rho) T, E[log mean_i e^{eps_i}] ~= s^2/2 (1-1/N) to first order = gamma* T. So E[log W_CM - log W_BH] ~= 0 under iid; > 0 only via saturation over long horizons (bounded by log N) or cross-sectional mean reversion at the rebalance horizon; < 0 under cross-sectional momentum. Arithmetic (the repo's per-decision unit): E[r_CM] = sum wbar_i alpha_i; E[r_BH] = sum E[w_t,i] alpha_i >= E[r_CM] when drifts differ => long-CM/short-BH has E <= 0 under iid; its positive backtests are mean-reversion bets.
2022 CONCENTRATION ARITHMETIC. CoinGecko BTC.D incl. stables 37.9% (2022-01-01) -> 38.6% (12-31); stables $167.9B of ~$2.25T (7.4%) -> ~$140B of ~$0.80T (~17%) => ex-stable BTC share 0.379/0.926 = 40.9% -> 0.386/0.83 = 46.5% (+5.6 pp). Implied: ex-stable market x0.32 (-68%), BTC x0.36 (-64%), ETH x0.33 (-67%), cap-weighted alts ex-ETH x0.29 (-71%); equal-weight Kraken alt basket ~x0.20 (-80%: SOL -94, AVAX -90, DOT -84, ADA -81, FIL -91, SAND -93, MANA -92, LUNA -100 vs LTC -52, XRP -59, DOGE -59). SPT: log(Z_pi/Z_mu)(T) = log(D_p(mu_T)/D_p(mu_0)) + (1-p) int gamma*_pi dt. Stylised market BTC 0.41, ETH 0.19, 38 alts x 0.0105 -> BTC 0.465, ETH 0.17, alts 0.0066 (log -0.47). EW (p->0): drift = mean log share change = (0.126 - 0.111 + 38*(-0.467))/40 = -0.44; gamma*_EW(2022, sigma~1.0, rho~0.7) ~ +0.15 => relative -0.30, EW absolute ~ x0.32*e^{-0.30} = x0.24 (-76%). Diversity p=0.5: weights prop to sqrt(mu) => BTC 12.9%, ETH 8.8%, alts 78% (already alt-heavy for N=40); D_{1/2} = (sum sqrt mu)^2: 24.75 -> 17.47 (log -0.35); +(1-p)gamma* ~ +0.05 => -0.30. Direct check: 0.129*0.36 + 0.088*0.33 + 0.78*0.20 = 0.232 vs market 0.319 => log -0.32 (consistent). Dollar-neutral unit-gross long-FGP/short-market: ~ -15% in 2022 before costs. 2018: BTC.D ~35% -> ~52%, same sign. Shannon 50/50 BTC/USD in 2022: BTC log -1.02, sigma~0.65 => alpha ~ -0.81; CM growth 0.5*(-0.81) - 0.5*0.25*0.42 = -0.458 (-37%) vs 50/50 B&H 0.5*0.36 + 0.5 = 0.68 (-32%): the demon loses to B&H in a trending bear.
SCORER CAVEAT. trader/backtest.py:221-223 computes gross = sum pos*(log c_{t+H} - log c_t) = weighted-average constituent LOG return, which omits gamma* exactly (PORTFOLIO_RESULT.md flagged assumption 3 says so). For a 40-coin 1/N long at 3.5%/day the omitted term ~ 1/2 sum w sigma_d^2 ~ 6 bp/day ~ 2.2%/yr ~ +0.3 Sharpe-equivalent: the record's 1/N 'B&H' -0.40 FULL PIT reads ~ -0.1 in simple-return terms, BEAR22 -2.54 ~ -2.2. No sign changes.

bear_positive_without_forecast.argument: Long-only versions: absolute return = market beta + gamma*; gamma* (~7%/yr in 2022 conditions) cannot offset a -68% ex-stable market, and the record already measures the daily-rebalanced 1/N PIT book at gross per-decision Sharpe -2.54 in BEAR22 and -2.28 in BEAR18 (runs/819_single_asset/POWERED_RESULT.md, B&H column, which is a daily 1/n_present reset — trader/backtest.py:225-227). Shannon 50/50 BTC/cash loses ~37% in 2022 and underperforms the 50/50 B&H (-32%) because it buys all the way down. Long-short 'relative arbitrage' (long diversity- or equal-weighted, short cap-weighted market): its log relative return = diversity-drift term + (1-p) gamma*; the drift term is a bet that concentration will not rise, i.e. a forecast on BTC dominance, and in both bears on record ex-stablecoin BTC dominance rose (2018 ~35%->52%; 2022 ~41%->46.5%) while small alts fell ~80% vs BTC -64%, giving ~ -0.30 log relative in 2022 (-15% dollar-neutral) before costs. The only mechanism that makes any version positive in expectation versus its benchmark is cross-sectional mean reversion at the rebalance horizon, which is a forecast (Chambers-Zdanowicz 2014; Hallerbach 2014), and the crypto evidence places daily reversal in illiquid small coins (<10% of cap) and daily momentum in the largest ones (Zaremba et al. 2021). There is no version of this family that is BEAR-positive in absolute terms without a forecast.

honest_odds: P(clearing the goalposts as written — net@21 >= +0.97 on unseen 2024-2026, hold positions, BEAR-positive) ~ 1-2%. Reasoning: (i) every long-only version has absolute Sharpe = beta Sharpe + a variance-only benefit; the record measures the daily 1/N PIT book at gross -0.40 FULL / -2.54 BEAR22 / -1.63 CHOP25 / -0.29 BULL24 and the ~+0.3 Sharpe-equivalent scorer omission cannot lift it; BEAR-positivity is impossible for a long-only book in a -68% year. (ii) long-short relative books have zero expected arithmetic return under iid, negative under momentum, and lose whenever concentration rises — ex-stable BTC dominance rose in 2018, 2022 and every year 2023-2025 (avg 45.6% -> 51.9% -> 59.3%), so the drift term has been negative in 5 of the last 8 years including both bears. (iii) the only route to positive expectation vs benchmark is cross-sectional mean reversion at the rebalance horizon — a forecast, and the crypto evidence places daily reversal in illiquid small coins where 897's adverse selection sits, with daily momentum among the large coins. Why not 0%: a 273-asset long-short book can post +0.97 over a 2.5-year window by luck, and the small-cap tail may carry an illiquidity-reversal premium the dollar-volume proxy would pick up. Side odds: P(PF2 premium vs true B&H positive on the growth criterion) ~ 30% (2020-21 rotation for; 2018-19 dead-coin buying and 2022-25 rising dominance against); P(any long-only version BEAR22 > 0) ~ 0% (already measured); P(B7 BEAR22 > 0) <= 10%.
open_doubts: Path dependence of the drift term: ex-stable BTC dominance inside the repo's BEAR22 window went ~45% (2021-11-10) -> ~41% (Jan 2022) -> ~55% (Jun 2022) -> ~46.5% (Dec 2022); my -0.30 uses calendar-2022 endpoints. Sign is robust, magnitude is +-0.1, and a weekly/banded rebalance samples the path differently.

Kraken PIT universe is not the global market: 273 assets with a thick micro-cap tail; a p=0.5 diversity book on 273 assets would be ~90% micro-caps, and dollar-volume weights are not market caps. Liquidity/adverse selection at 21 bp is not modelled — second-order at ~7x/yr turnover (897's 5 bp term ~0.35%/yr) but not zero for the tail.
